aidb_assessment.novelty: The paper’s distinctive contribution is a four-action decision boundary that separates durable persistence, ephemeral use, externally authoritative verification, and user-authoritative clarification, then tests both labels and structured memory operations. The independently adjudicated evidence-flip and naturalistic extensions strengthen the benchmark design, although the core scenarios remain authored and structurally predictable.
aidb_assessment.rationale: The benchmark targets a practically important, under-measured failure boundary and reports unusually candid negative results and validity constraints. The frozen artifact appears suitable for replication and internal policy testing. Adoption as a definitive benchmark should wait for matched label/tool prompts, evaluation of the complete policy, larger naturalistic clarification samples, and end-to-end outcome measurements.
aidb_assessment.usefulness: Useful as an auditable diagnostic suite for memory-gate policies and especially for detecting erroneous persistence or label/tool inconsistencies. It should not be treated as a deployment-readiness test because it does not execute memory systems, measure downstream utility, or establish privacy and interaction costs.

executive_summary: The paper introduces MCB, a benchmark for deciding whether interaction-derived information should be persisted, used ephemerally, externally verified, or clarified with the user at reuse time. Its strongest evidence is an independently adjudicated held-out set plus controlled prompt and label-versus-tool comparisons. Prompting materially helps some models, but clarification remains difficult. Tool-selection behavior can diverge sharply from label decisions, although unmatched prompts prevent causal attribution to interface alone. The work is valuable as a diagnostic benchmark, not evidence that any memory backend or end-to-end agent is safe or useful.

assumptions: The annotation policy intentionally prefers weaker commitment when persistence remains uncertain.
Reuse context is known when the model decides; findings do not transfer automatically to acquisition-time gating.
User intent, preferences, and referents are user-authoritative, whereas changing facts, versions, and schedules are externally authoritative.
The benchmark labels operationalize a stated conservative policy, not universal ground truth.
Bootstrap intervals characterize uncertainty over evaluated items, not repeated stochastic model sampling.
key_components: Each scenario supplies acquisition context, a candidate update, and a visible later reuse context.
The four actions distinguish durable commitment, local use, world-authoritative verification, and user-authoritative clarification.
Two non-authors label the held-out primary and contrast sets independently; a blind third annotator resolves disagreements.
MCB-Act replaces labels with one structured call among memory_write, use_now, check_source, and ask_user.
Prompt conditions comprise bare definitions, the original five-rule policy, and four development demonstrations.
The evidence-flip extension changes evidence within paired, rule-authored scenarios; the naturalistic extension uses screened public user turns and a standardized later context.
method.overview: MCB frames memory handling as four-way classification over persist, ephemeral, verify, and clarify. The primary benchmark is split into development and held-out portions; a rule-authored evidence-flip contrast set tests controlled sensitivity, and a small WildChat-derived extension provides a descriptive naturalistic check. Four checkpoints are evaluated with bare definitions, an archived policy prompt, few-shot examples, and a structured tool-selection condition. Held-out labels are independently audited, and analyses include action-level metrics, bootstrap intervals, exact paired tests, and exploratory class-recall comparisons.

open_questions: How do fully guide-aligned label and tool prompts compare when decision rules, examples, wording, and role framing are matched?
Does the verification-versus-clarification gap survive on larger naturalistic samples with balanced actions and matched item difficulty?
How should application-specific costs of erroneous persistence, missed persistence, unnecessary questions, and external verification be calibrated?
Do MCB improvements translate into fewer harmful writes and better downstream retrieval or task outcomes in real memory backends?
How robust are the findings across repeated serving, decoding settings, quantization levels, languages, domains, and model families?

problem.importance: A mistaken durable update can silently affect future behavior, while world facts, user intent, scope, and referents require different authorities. A memory system therefore needs a decision boundary before treating interaction-derived information as durable.
problem.scope: The study evaluates reuse-time action selection under a conservative policy. It does not evaluate candidate extraction, acquisition-time filtering, actual writes, external checks, user answers, retrieval, or downstream task utility.
problem.statement: Given interaction history, a candidate memory update, and a later reuse context, determine whether the candidate warrants durable persistence, current-context use only, an external check, or clarification from the user.

proposed_experiments.baseline: For each checkpoint, compare the archived bare-label and original tool runs against matched complete-policy label and act-plus-policy runs on the same adjudicated primary and contrast items.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: With identical complete decision rules, examples, and role framing, label and tool outputs will show substantially higher agreement than the archived unmatched settings without increasing erroneous persistence.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Paired label–tool agreement, with accuracy and over-memory as co-reported safety metrics.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop after all preregistered checkpoints complete deterministic parsing and paired tests; reject the hypothesis if agreement does not improve or if over-memory worsens under the matched tool condition.

proposed_experiments.baseline: The original held-out verify and clarify subsets, evaluated with the same checkpoints and a fully guide-aligned prompt.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Verification recall will no longer consistently exceed clarification recall after balancing classes and matching scenario difficulty, authority cues, lexical traps, and ambiguity strength.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Within-model difference between verify recall and clarify recall, with multiplicity-corrected paired or stratified inference on a newly adjudicated balanced set.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop at the preregistered sample size or earlier only for annotation-quality failure; reject the hypothesis if the corrected recall gap remains consistently positive across model families.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Always-Persist, the archived policy gate, and a matched complete-policy gate connected to the same memory backend and retrieval pipeline.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: A reuse-time gate using the complete policy reduces harmful durable writes while preserving downstream task utility compared with unconditional persistence and the archived policy.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Rate of harmful durable updates measured on subsequent tasks, jointly reported with downstream task success and user-intervention burden.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop after the preregistered longitudinal task set; reject the hypothesis if harmful writes do not decrease, or if task success or intervention burden crosses predefined non-inferiority limits.

reproducibility.assessment: Reproducibility of the frozen numerical analyses is strong: the archive reportedly contains data, annotations, prompts, predictions, metadata, tests, and a script that regenerates the analyses without model access. Reproduction of live model behavior and extensions beyond the archived prompts is only partial because there is no claimed public repository, the aligned policy is unevaluated, and backend execution is outside scope.

Fresh model inference for hosted checkpoints may depend on external access and serving behavior.
The complete guide-aligned label and tool policies have no reported runs.
No repeated-seed or repeated-serving robustness study is reported.
No executable end-to-end memory backend, source-check, or user-clarification evaluation is reported.
